NVlabs/vla-perf:
VLA-Perf is a performance analysis tool for vision-language-action models.
It models inference latency across neural network architectures and network interfaces.
The tool helps engineers select hardware and optimize model latency before robot deployment.
It operates on Linux workstations, data center servers, and NVIDIA Jetson edge systems.
NVlabs/PointWorld:
PointWorld is a 3D world model for robotic manipulation tasks.
It predicts full-scene 3D point flows from RGB-D observations and robot actions.
The model enables robots to predict physical object motions in unmapped environments.
It runs on workstation GPUs and in simulated environments like Isaac Lab.
NVlabs/alpamayo1.5:
Alpamayo 1.5 is an open 10-billion parameter vision-language-action model for autonomous vehicles.
It combines visual question answering with reinforcement learning for interactive driving decisions.
The model produces steerable reasoning traces to justify vehicle trajectories.
It operates on vehicle compute platforms and GPU training clusters.
NVlabs/GEM-X:
GEM-X is a 3D human motion estimation model for robotic imitation.
It extracts whole-body poses from monocular video using the SOMA body model.
The model converts human demonstrations into robot joint trajectories without motion-capture markers.
It executes on CUDA GPUs and retargets motions to Unitree humanoid robots.
NVlabs/GR00T-VisualSim2Real:
GR00T-VisualSim2Real is a simulation-to-real transfer framework for humanoid loco-manipulation.
It trains control policies in Isaac Sim using RGB cameras and proprioceptive sensors.
The framework enables zero-shot policy deployment on physical humanoid robots without manual tuning.
It trains in Isaac Sim and deploys on physical Unitree G1 humanoid robots.
NVlabs/alpamayo-recipes:
Alpamayo Recipes is a developer toolkit for autonomous vehicle foundation models.
It provides scripts for supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and model quantization.
Developers use these recipes to train and adapt Alpamayo models for custom fleets.
It operates on NVIDIA GPU clusters and Linux development workstations.
NVlabs/alpagym:
AlpaGym is a reinforcement learning harness for end-to-end autonomous driving policies.
It runs driving policies in closed-loop simulations using AlpaSim and Cosmos-RL.
The system allows policies to learn directly from the consequences of their actions.
It executes on distributed GPU clusters connected to simulation environments.
NVlabs/alpamayo-coc-autolabeler:
Alpamayo CoC Autolabeler is an automated data labeling pipeline for autonomous vehicles.
It extracts meta-actions and chain-of-causation reasoning labels from raw driving video clips.
The pipeline removes manual labeling costs while generating structured causal explanations for training.
It runs on data center GPU servers processing recorded vehicle sensor logs.
NVlabs/alpamayo2:
Alpamayo 2 is a 34-billion parameter multi-task foundation model for autonomous driving.
It pairs a vision-language backbone with a diffusion expert to generate motion trajectories.
The model provides end-to-end driving decisions with verifiable chain-of-causation reasoning.
It executes on cloud GPU clusters and vehicle computing platforms.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-predict1:
Cosmos-Predict1 is a world foundation model for physical artificial intelligence applications.
It generates future video frames and physical states from initial visual observations.
The model allows embodied agents to simulate physical outcomes before executing real actions.
It operates on NVIDIA data center GPUs and within robotic simulation frameworks.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-transfer1:
Cosmos-Transfer1 is a domain transfer model for physical artificial intelligence.
It transforms simulated visual environments into realistic sensor observations.
The model reduces the perceptual domain gap between simulation and the real world.
It operates on cloud GPU systems supporting robotic simulation pipelines.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-reason1:
Cosmos-Reason1 is a multimodal reasoning model for physical artificial intelligence.
It applies chain-of-thought processing to analyze physical interactions and spatial relationships.
The model provides common-sense physical reasoning to improve robot decision-making accuracy.
It runs on server GPUs and connects to autonomous agent control pipelines.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-xenna:
Cosmos-Xenna is a distributed data processing library for physical artificial intelligence.
It builds scalable dataset pipelines using the Ray distributed execution framework.
The library accelerates video and sensor data preparation for world model training.
It operates on multi-node GPU clusters and cloud compute infrastructure.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-rl:
Cosmos-RL is a distributed reinforcement learning framework for physical artificial intelligence.
It coordinates distributed policy rollouts and model updates across GPU clusters.
The framework accelerates policy learning in complex physical environments and simulations.
It runs on high-performance compute clusters linked to simulators like Isaac Lab.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-predict2:
Cosmos-Predict2 is a second-generation world foundation model for physical artificial intelligence.
It generates high-resolution future video states from text instructions and visual inputs.
The model improves physical realism and visual fidelity in synthetic world simulations.
It runs on NVIDIA Tensor Core GPUs in cloud and data center environments.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-dependencies:
Cosmos Dependencies provides dependency specifications and build environments for Cosmos models.
It defines software packages, container configurations, and library versions for Cosmos workflows.
The repository ensures consistent environments across development and production deployments.
It configures Linux workstations, Docker containers, and high-performance computing clusters.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-cookbook:
Cosmos Cookbook is a collection of reference recipes for NVIDIA Cosmos models.
It provides scripts and sample workflows for post-training, fine-tuning, and inference.
Developers use these recipes to customize foundation models for specific robotic domains.
It operates on NVIDIA GPU servers and cloud training environments.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-reason2:
Cosmos-Reason2 is an advanced physical reasoning foundation model for embodied agents.
It processes multimodal visual data to predict physical consequences through extended chain-of-thought reasoning.
The model enhances spatial comprehension and common-sense logic for complex robot tasks.
It runs on enterprise GPU servers and autonomous system inference backends.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-predict2.5:
Cosmos-Predict2.5 is a video-based world foundation model for physical environment simulation.
It predicts future video frames with physical consistency from image and prompt inputs.
The model generates realistic training scenarios for autonomous vehicles and humanoid robots.
It operates on large-scale GPU training and inference clusters.
nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-transfer2.5:
Cosmos-Transfer2.5 is a controlled world transfer model for physical artificial intelligence.
It conditions video generation on spatial controls like depth maps and segmentation masks.
The model generates diverse, physics-grounded training environments from controlled geometric inputs.
It runs on data center GPUs supporting simulation and synthetic data generation.
triton-inference-server/server:
Triton Inference Server is an open-source serving system for deep learning models.
It executes concurrent model inferences across multiple framework backends with dynamic batching.
The server maximizes GPU hardware utilization and minimizes latency in production deployments.
It runs in data centers, cloud instances, and NVIDIA Jetson edge devices.
triton-inference-server/common:
Triton Common is a shared utility library for Triton Inference Server components.
It provides common data structures, logging interfaces, and error handling mechanisms.
The library ensures uniform architecture and code reuse across all Triton backends.
It compiles into Triton server binaries on Linux and Jetson systems.
triton-inference-server/backend:
Triton Backend is the developer framework and C++ interface for Triton model execution.
It provides APIs to manage model lifecycles, memory buffers, and inference requests.
Developers use this framework to build custom execution backends for specialized runtimes.
It operates inside the Triton Inference Server runtime environment on GPU hosts.
triton-inference-server/onnxruntime_back:
Triton ONNX Runtime Backend is an execution plugin for ONNX models in Triton.
It routes inference requests directly into the ONNX Runtime engine using CPU or GPU execution providers.
The backend enables fast serving of standardized ONNX models without framework-specific conversion.
It operates inside Triton Inference Server containers on cloud and edge GPUs.
triton-inference-server/python_backend:
Triton Python Backend is an execution runtime for Python code within Triton.
It executes Python model logic, custom preprocessing, and postprocessing through inter-process communication.
Developers can serve Python pipelines in Triton without writing native C++ code.
It runs within Triton Inference Server on workstations, cloud instances, and Jetson systems.
triton-inference-server/model_analyzer:
Triton Model Analyzer is a profiling and benchmarking tool for Triton models.
It measures latency, throughput, and memory consumption across various concurrency configurations.
The tool identifies optimal batch sizes and instance counts to maximize GPU efficiency.
It operates as a command-line tool on Linux hosts connected to Triton servers.
triton-inference-server/dali_backend:
Triton DALI Backend is an execution plugin for data preprocessing within Triton.
It runs NVIDIA Data Loading Library pipelines directly on GPUs before model inference.
The backend offloads intensive data transformation from host CPUs to accelerate pipeline throughput.
It runs inside Triton Inference Server on NVIDIA GPU servers and Jetson devices.
triton-inference-server/tensorflow_backe:
Triton TensorFlow Backend is a model execution plugin for TensorFlow models.
It loads and runs TensorFlow GraphDef and SavedModel formats using the TensorFlow C API.
The backend provides high-performance serving for TensorFlow models without manual format conversion.
It executes inside Triton Inference Server on cloud instances and edge compute nodes.
triton-inference-server/core:
Triton Core is the fundamental library implementing Triton Inference Server functionality.
It manages model repositories, schedules incoming requests, and orchestrates backend execution.
The library provides the core inference engine required by all Triton frontends and backends.
It builds into Triton server runtimes on Linux servers and Jetson embedded computers.
triton-inference-server/pytorch_backend:
Triton PyTorch Backend is an execution plugin for PyTorch models in Triton.
It loads and evaluates TorchScript models using the LibTorch C++ API.
The backend enables native PyTorch model serving with GPU acceleration and dynamic batching.
It runs inside Triton Inference Server on Linux servers and Jetson hardware.
triton-inference-server/fil_backend:
Triton FIL Backend is an inference plugin for tree-based machine learning models.
It evaluates decision trees, random forests, and gradient-boosted models using the Forest Inference Library.
The backend accelerates classical machine learning inference on GPUs by several orders of magnitude.
It operates within Triton Inference Server on workstation and data center GPUs.
triton-inference-server/tensorrt_backend:
Triton TensorRT Backend is a high-performance execution plugin for NVIDIA TensorRT engines.
It executes optimized TensorRT plan files directly on NVIDIA GPU hardware.
The backend delivers the lowest latency and highest throughput for deep learning inference.
It operates inside Triton Inference Server across desktop GPUs, cloud servers, and Jetson platforms.
triton-inference-server/client:
Triton Client is a collection of client libraries for Triton Inference Server.
It sends inference requests and receives predictions over HTTP, gRPC, and shared memory.
Applications use these libraries to communicate efficiently with Triton servers from various programming languages.
It runs on client systems, robot host computers, and embedded devices in C++, Python, or Java.
triton-inference-server/model_navigator:
Triton Model Navigator is an automated optimization and deployment tool for machine learning models.
It profiles models across export formats, quantization precisions, and execution runtimes.
The tool automates the search for the fastest model configuration on target hardware.
It executes on local workstations and cloud compute instances with NVIDIA GPUs.
triton-inference-server/pytriton:
PyTriton is a Python library that connects Python code directly to Triton Inference Server.
It exposes Python functions and models as Triton endpoints using a simple decorator API.
Developers can deploy Triton inference services from existing Python applications without writing configuration files.
It runs on local development machines, cloud servers, and GPU edge nodes.
triton-inference-server/tutorials:
Triton Tutorials is a repository of educational guides and examples for Triton Inference Server.
It provides step-by-step instructions, sample code, and notebooks for model deployment and optimization.
The repository helps engineers learn Triton concepts and implement production inference architectures quickly.
It runs in Jupyter notebook environments, local workstations, and cloud development containers.
triton-inference-server/tensorrtllm_back:
Triton TensorRT-LLM Backend is a specialized runtime plugin for serving large language models.
It utilizes TensorRT-LLM to execute multi-GPU tensor-parallel inference with in-flight batching.
The backend maximizes throughput and reduces response times for generative language model serving.
It operates inside Triton Inference Server on multi-GPU server nodes and workstations.
triton-inference-server/triton_cli:
Triton CLI is a command-line interface for managing Triton Inference Server workflows.
It automates model repository creation, container startup, and endpoint performance profiling.
Developers use this tool to test and deploy models without complex manual setup.
It runs in terminal environments on Linux developer workstations and cloud virtual machines.
nvidia-isaac/kaya-robot:
Kaya is an open-source three-wheeled holonomic mobile robot platform.
It utilizes three omnidirectional wheels driven by smart servos under Isaac SDK software control.
The platform provides an accessible reference hardware design for robotics education and development.
It operates on physical mobile robot bases powered by NVIDIA Jetson Nano computers.
nvidia-isaac/velodyne_lidar:
Velodyne LiDAR is a hardware driver integration package for the NVIDIA Isaac SDK.
It ingests Ethernet packet streams from Velodyne LiDAR sensors and outputs structured point clouds.
The driver provides reliable 3D perception data for robot localization and obstacle avoidance pipelines.
It runs on NVIDIA Jetson embedded computers mounted on autonomous mobile robots.
nvidia-isaac/sick_lidar_tim571:
SICK TiM571 is a 2D LiDAR driver module for the NVIDIA Isaac SDK.
It connects to the SICK TiM571 sensor over Ethernet to stream planar laser scans.
The module supplies accurate distance measurements for mobile robot navigation and safety monitoring.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge computers installed on industrial mobile robots.
nvidia-isaac/econ_camera_steereocam:
e-con STEEReoCAM is a stereo camera driver package for the NVIDIA Isaac SDK.
It captures synchronized stereo image pairs and IMU sensor data over MIPI interfaces.
The driver provides synchronized visual-inertial data for accurate depth estimation and visual odometry.
It runs on NVIDIA Jetson Xavier and Jetson Nano embedded developer kits.
nvidia-isaac/lips_AE400:
LIPSedge AE400 is an industrial stereo depth camera driver for the NVIDIA Isaac SDK.
It streams RGB frames and depth maps over Gigabit Ethernet connections into Isaac applications.
The driver delivers rugged 3D perception data for industrial robot navigation and object detection.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson computers integrated into industrial automation robots.
nvidia-isaac/laikago_lidar_mount:
Laikago LiDAR Mount is a collection of mechanical CAD designs for quadruped robots.
It provides 3D-printable bracket models designed to secure Velodyne VLP-16 sensors on robot chassis.
The mount provides stable sensor placement to capture unobstructed 3D scans during robot movement.
It installs directly onto physical Unitree Laikago quadruped robot bodies.
nvidia-isaac/sick_safetyscanners_isaac:
SICK Safety Scanners Isaac is a safety sensor integration layer for Isaac SDK.
It reads safety zone status and scan data from SICK laser safety devices.
The integration enables autonomous mobile robots to comply with industrial collision-prevention standards.
It operates on Jetson edge computers in industrial AGV and AMR vehicles.
nvidia-isaac/nvblox:
nvblox is a GPU-accelerated 3D volumetric mapping library for robotics.
It constructs Truncated Signed Distance Fields and Euclidean Distance Fields from depth images using CUDA.
The library provides real-time distance queries and obstacle representations for motion planning and navigation.
It runs on NVIDIA Jetson embedded modules and workstation GPUs.
nvidia-isaac/isaac_mission_dispatch:
Isaac Mission Dispatch is a cloud fleet management service for autonomous mobile robots.
It assigns tasks and communicates with edge robots using the open VDA5050 protocol standard.
The service orchestrates multi-robot warehouse operations and ensures coordinated mission execution.
It operates in cloud environments and on-premises server infrastructure.
nvidia-isaac/ota-file-service:
OTA File Service is a cloud service for robot software and file distribution.
It provides REST APIs to upload, manage, and deploy software updates to remote robots.
The service simplifies remote fleet maintenance and ensures consistent software versions across machines.
It runs on cloud servers and connects to networked robots in the field.
nvidia-isaac/cuVSLAM:
cuVSLAM is a CUDA-accelerated visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping library.
It processes stereo camera images and IMU measurements to estimate 3D robot poses.
The library provides low-latency, drift-free robot localization without expensive external tracking systems.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge computers and workstation GPUs.
nvidia-isaac/SWAGGER:
SWAGGER is a topological path planning tool for autonomous mobile robots.
It generates sparse waypoint graphs from 2D occupancy grid maps using geometric pruning.
The tool reduces path search complexity to enable fast global routing across large facilities.
It runs on robot host computers and fleet management servers in Python.
nvidia-isaac/isaac_mission_control:
Isaac Mission Control is a lightweight fleet management coordinator for mobile robots.
It orchestrates VDA5050-compliant mission dispatch services and monitors vehicle statuses in real time.
The coordinator provides centralized task scheduling and traffic management for automated logistics.
It runs on enterprise servers and cloud platforms managing robot fleets.
nvidia-isaac/pyCuSFM:
pyCuSFM is a Python interface for CUDA-accelerated Structure-from-Motion algorithms.
It estimates camera poses and reconstructs sparse 3D point clouds using parallel GPU solvers.
The package accelerates large-scale 3D scene reconstruction from collections of visual images.
It runs on workstation and data center GPUs running Python 3.
nvidia-isaac/WBC-AGILE:
WBC-AGILE is a reinforcement learning framework for humanoid robot loco-manipulation.
It combines whole-body control algorithms with GPU-parallel training in Isaac Lab.
The framework enables humanoid robots to balance while executing complex manipulation tasks.
It runs in Isaac Lab simulation and deploys onto physical humanoid robots.
nvidia-isaac/nvblox_mindmap:
nvblox_mindmap is a spatial memory framework for robot manipulation policies.
It fuses deep neural feature maps with nvblox 3D volumetric representations in real time.
The framework gives robots persistent 3D semantic memory to locate objects in cluttered spaces.
It operates in Isaac Lab simulations and on GPU-equipped physical robots.
nvidia-isaac/cumotion:
cuMotion is a GPU-accelerated motion planning library for robot manipulators.
It computes collision-free trajectories using massively parallel CUDA kinematics algorithms.
The library generates reactive robot trajectories in milliseconds to avoid dynamic obstacles.
It runs on NVIDIA Jetson edge platforms and workstation GPUs.
nvidia-isaac/video_to_data:
Video to Data is a data generation pipeline for robotic manipulation.
It converts RGB human demonstration videos into simulation-ready 3D trajectories and robot assets.
The pipeline eliminates costly physical robot teleoperation by turning human videos into training data.
It operates on GPU workstations and cloud servers integrated with Isaac Sim.
nvidia-isaac/cuNLS:
cuNLS is a CUDA-accelerated nonlinear least-squares optimization solver for robotics.
It solves factor graphs and manifold optimization problems using parallel Gauss-Newton iterations.
The solver delivers real-time optimization performance for SLAM, bundle adjustment, and calibration tasks.
It executes on NVIDIA GPUs in edge devices and high-performance workstations.
nvidia-isaac/leapp:
LEAPP is an export and deployment library for PyTorch robot policy pipelines.
It traces multi-step computational graphs and generates annotated deployment artifacts.
The library simplifies policy export from research code to optimized production inference runtimes.
It runs on Python development workstations and targets embedded robotic computers.
nvidia-isaac/gr00t-leapp-export:
gr00t-leapp-export is an export utility for NVIDIA Isaac GR00T foundation policies.
It applies LEAPP annotations to convert GR00T neural network models into deployable formats.
The utility streamlines the transition of humanoid foundation policies from training to real-world robots.
It operates on GPU training servers and packages policies for edge deployment.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-perf-tools:
Holoscan Performance Tools is a benchmarking suite for NVIDIA Holoscan streaming applications.
It measures pipeline throughput, operator execution times, and end-to-end data latency.
The tools help developers identify pipeline bottlenecks and optimize real-time streaming performance.
It runs on NVIDIA IGX systems and Jetson edge compute devices.
nvidia-holoscan/meta-tegra-holoscan:
meta-tegra-holoscan is an OpenEmbedded and Yocto board support package layer.
It provides build recipes to compile customized Linux images for Holoscan developer kits.
The layer allows engineers to build production-grade, secure embedded operating systems with GPU support.
It executes on Linux build hosts targeting NVIDIA IGX and Jetson hardware.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-sdk:
Holoscan SDK is a software development kit for low-latency AI sensor processing.
It builds streaming pipelines that transfer sensor data directly to GPUs using RDMA.
The SDK delivers real-time AI inference and stream processing for mission-critical sensor applications.
It runs on NVIDIA IGX systems, Jetson platforms, and Clara medical devices.
nvidia-holoscan/holohub:
HoloHub is the central community repository for the NVIDIA Holoscan ecosystem.
It provides reference applications, reusable pipeline operators, and step-by-step developer tutorials.
The repository accelerates development of medical imaging, robotics, and industrial sensing workflows.
It operates across Linux developer workstations, NVIDIA IGX, and Jetson systems.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-docs:
Holoscan Docs is the official documentation repository for the NVIDIA Holoscan platform.
It hosts architecture guides, API references, and deployment tutorials in structured source formats.
The documentation provides essential technical instructions for engineers building real-time sensor pipelines.
It builds into web documentation hosted on the NVIDIA developer portal.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-test-suite:
Holoscan Test Suite is a verification and validation framework for Holoscan platforms.
It executes automated hardware diagnostics and publishes test results through a lightweight web server.
The framework ensures system stability and regulatory compliance before clinical and industrial deployments.
It runs on NVIDIA IGX medical hardware and industrial edge systems.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-sensor-bridge:
Holoscan Sensor Bridge is a low-latency FPGA sensor interface for NVIDIA GPUs.
It captures raw peripheral sensor streams and transmits packets over Ethernet directly into GPU memory.
The bridge eliminates CPU bottlenecks to enable microsecond-level sensor data ingestion for AI processing.
It connects FPGA hardware interfaces to NVIDIA IGX and Jetson compute units.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-federated-analy:
Holoscan Federated Analytics is a distributed data analytics framework for edge devices.
It aggregates operational telemetry and model metrics across distributed devices without sharing raw data.
The framework preserves data privacy while enabling fleet-wide performance monitoring and improvements.
It operates on networked Holoscan edge devices and centralized analytics servers.
nvidia-holoscan/holoscan-cli:
Holoscan CLI is a command-line utility for managing Holoscan applications.
It provides commands to build, containerize, run, and test HoloHub operators and applications.
The CLI streamlines the development and deployment process for real-time sensor processing pipelines.
It executes in terminal environments on Linux developer workstations and edge platforms.
NVIDIA/cuopt-examples:
cuOpt Examples is a collection of reference implementations for NVIDIA cuOpt.
It demonstrates GPU-accelerated algorithms for vehicle routing, linear programming, and logistics scheduling.
The examples help developers solve complex combinatorial optimization problems in seconds instead of hours.
It runs on CUDA-enabled workstations and enterprise GPU servers using Python.
rapidsai/cuspatial:
cuSpatial is a GPU-accelerated GIS and spatiotemporal analysis library.
It executes parallel spatial indexing, trajectory clustering, and polygon distance queries using CUDA.
The library accelerates geospatial calculations by orders of magnitude compared to CPU-based GIS tools.
It operates on NVIDIA GPU workstations and cloud computing instances.
rapidsai/cusignal:
cuSignal is a GPU-accelerated signal processing library within the RAPIDS ecosystem.
It provides CUDA implementations of standard SciPy signal processing functions and filtering algorithms.
The library delivers substantial speedups for high-throughput sensor and radar signal processing pipelines.
It runs on CUDA-enabled workstations and edge GPU computing platforms.
rapidsai/cugraph:
cuGraph is a GPU-accelerated graph analytics library within the RAPIDS ecosystem.
It executes parallel graph algorithms for PageRank, community detection, and shortest paths using CUDA.
The library enables fast exploration and analysis of massive graphs containing billions of edges.
It operates on single-GPU workstations and multi-node GPU clusters.
NVIDIA/cudf:
cuDF is a GPU-accelerated DataFrame library for tabular data processing.
It implements pandas-compatible DataFrame operations directly on GPU memory using CUDA kernels.
The library eliminates CPU data manipulation bottlenecks in machine learning and analytics workflows.
It runs on Linux workstations and enterprise cloud GPU environments.
rapidsai/rmm:
RMM is a high-performance GPU memory management library for CUDA applications.
It provides configurable memory allocation pools and caching allocators for CUDA device memory.
The library reduces memory allocation overhead and prevents fragmentation during intensive GPU computations.
It integrates into C++ and Python applications running on NVIDIA GPUs.
